An ancient and powerful energy flows through these places, concentrating in hidden, inexhaustible sources. Controlling this power allows one to bend to their will life's most important aspect: time, and the rhythms it imprints on the environment and every being. Echoes of Time is a strategic game for 2-4 players in which you attempt to create the best-equipped fellowship of characters from different factions to conquer the sources of power. Try to control and modify the flow of time to outshine your opponents. The game includes more than one hundred cards with unique effects that you will use to build a new deck each game, and a "sliding tile" system guides you in managing the time needed for your cards to become usable, while simultaneously controlling the activation rhythm of their effects. And I got a very nice set of cards put together to play during the demo. Played 2 of them, got some points. I was very much looking forward to see the rest of them come in effect and activate combinations.  Then a guy conquered one of the goals for conquest, and made me lose 8 out of 10 cards, and 2 of out my 3 points in 2 rounds (I managed to play only one card after he started that). [Rating: 1/10] No fun... Too repetitive!  Also hard to comeback when someone has a lead (fortified place). And finally, it's subjective but I don't like the childish art (characters).

[Rating: 1/10] omg, if someone draws all the -vp cards or everyone else discard a card cards he/she can f*** everyone over big time. No fun.

[Rating: 2/10] Inspired by race for the galaxy but the implementation felt terrible. Extremely swingy cards and misleading objectives which seem to lack any balance.

[Rating: 3/10] I'm angry with this game. The premise of paying with time for actions and the puzzle which card I wish to play at a given time was charming, but when the game took place it was all ruined by weird card effects, unnecessary negative interaction, sources disbalance and necessity of discarding tons of cards. The game just doesn't want the player to play it :/

[Rating: 4/10] A generous 4, since I won't play again.  Some people won't like the interactive disruptions, including conquests and forced discards. Didn't bother me, but solitaire-oriented hobbyists will cry foul.  Has cool mechanics, but they're wrapped around an engine-builder. Not my style.  [i]Note:[/i] The players who stockpiled VP tokens regretted it, since they were continually trashed by card triggers.

[Rating: 4/10] Long player turns make it grinding. Play a card on a timeline and drive it off the timeline to activate the power. Small amount of eye poking and card stealing. Iconography. Meh.

[Rating: 4/10] I know there's an idea and great engine making, but it feels incredibly anticlimatic.
